relations.subject: Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
relations.evidence: In the following years of his youth he was tutored by Khenpo Thupten in grammar, astrology, Sanskrit and Buddhist texts.

relations.subject: Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
relations.evidence: At Shechen Monastery, he received a number of transmissions from Shechen Gyaltsap, who became one of his principal masters.

relations.subject: Dilgo Khyentse
relations.evidence: Thus he became a teacher and guide for Dilgo Khyentse, Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (2nd Dudjom Rinpoche) and Sogyal Rinpoche.

relations.subject: Jigdral Yeshe Dorje
relations.evidence: Thus he became a teacher and guide for Dilgo Khyentse, Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (2nd Dudjom Rinpoche) and Sogyal Rinpoche.

relations.subject: Sogyal Rinpoche
relations.evidence: Thus he became a teacher and guide for Dilgo Khyentse, Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (2nd Dudjom Rinpoche) and Sogyal Rinpoche.

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
relations.evidence: He was a major influence on a very young Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche, who first met him in 1945

relations.subject: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
relations.evidence: While there, he was invited to Tsurphu Monastery to give teachings and empowerments to Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, 16th Karmapa.

relations.subject: Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
relations.evidence: In turn, the Karmapa gave him an empowerment in the red form of Avalokiteśvara

relations.subject: Sangharakshita
relations.evidence: During this time he met Sangharakshita, who was then a monk living in Kalimpong. He bestowed on him four sadhanas - Avalokitesvara, Manjusri, Vajrapani, and Green Tāra.
